results.description: SCAFFOLD consistently outperforms FEDAVG in terms of MSE across all numbers of clients N ∈ {10, 100, 1000, 10000} and both linear and logistic regression.
results.evidence: results/formal/figure1-linear/summary.json and results/formal/figure1-logistic/summary.json contain final_mse_mean for each algorithm × n_agents combination. LINEAR REGRESSION: N=10 SCAFFOLD=58.95 < FEDAVG=176.54; N=100 SCAFFOLD=2.63 < FEDAVG=5.07; N=1000 SCAFFOLD=0.553 < FEDAVG=1.347; N=10000 SCAFFOLD=0.0457 < FEDAVG=0.1353. LOGISTIC REGRESSION: N=10 SCAFFOLD=0.02180 < FEDAVG=0.27731; N=100 SCAFFOLD=0.000879 < FEDAVG=0.06353; N=1000 SCAFFOLD=0.000182 < FEDAVG=0.02217; N=10000 SCAFFOLD=0.000135 < FEDAVG=0.01419. SCAFFOLD has strictly lower MSE than FEDAVG in all 8 (problem, N) combinations.
results.note: Comparison is based on final_mse_mean (the MSE at the last round). The stationary_tail_mse_mean values tell the same story consistently.

results.description: In linear regression, as the number of clients increases, the stationary MSE of SCAFFOLD decreases, with N=10000 achieving lower error than N=1000, N=1000 lower than N=100, and N=100 lower than N=10.
results.evidence: results/formal/figure1-linear/summary.json contains scaffold stationary_tail_mse_mean values: N=10 → 70.163, N=100 → 3.397, N=1000 → 0.545, N=10000 → 0.059. All three pairwise constraints hold (lower_is_better): N=10000 (0.059) < N=1000 (0.545) < N=100 (3.397) < N=10 (70.163).
results.note: Values used are stationary_tail_mse_mean (tail average of last 10 rounds), which is the appropriate stationary MSE measure. The ranking is unambiguous with large margins between each level.

results.description: In logistic regression, as the number of clients increases from 10 to 1000, the stationary MSE of SCAFFOLD decreases, with N=1000 lower than N=100 and N=100 lower than N=10.
results.evidence: results/formal/figure1-logistic/summary.json: SCAFFOLD stationary_tail_mse_mean values — N=10: 0.032463, N=100: 0.0007545, N=1000: 0.0001632. Both ordering constraints hold: 0.0001632 < 0.0007545 (N=1000 better than N=100) and 0.0007545 < 0.032463 (N=100 better than N=10). Metric is lower_is_better.
results.note: Values taken from stationary_tail_mse_mean (tail_rounds=10), which is the appropriate stationary/convergence metric. The decrease is monotonic and large in magnitude across all three N values.

results.description: In logistic regression, there is no improvement in stationary MSE from N=1000 to N=10000.
results.evidence: results/formal/figure1-logistic/summary.json: SCAFFOLD stationary_tail_mse_mean for N=1000 is 0.00016324223786852988, and for N=10000 is 0.00012612431792635647. The predicate stationary_mse(N=10000) >= stationary_mse(N=1000) is NOT satisfied: 0.000126 < 0.000163, meaning MSE improved (decreased) by ~22.7% when going from N=1000 to N=10000. The claim of "no improvement" is contradicted by the run outputs. Note also that the summary.json records scaffold_adjacent_client_ratios for 1000→10000 as observed_mse_ratio=1.2942962987030497, confirming a ~1.29x reduction (improvement) in MSE.
results.note: The scaffold_adjacent_client_ratios entry for from_n=1000 to to_n=10000 shows ratio=1.29, indicating the N=10000 MSE is lower than N=1000 MSE, directly contradicting the claim of no improvement.
